matters.title: Water Treatment Plant Filter Membrane Procurement
matters.text: Motion to authorize the purchase of equipment from FilmTec Corporation/ Memcor in the amount of $1,941,471.91

attachments.name: Sole Source
attachments.text:
Leading the Way
SINGLE / SOLE SOURCE JUSTIFICATION
Requesting Department: Public Works/ Utilities
Name of Requestor: Jeremy Lustig/ Utility Services Manager
1) Brief description of the requested product and its function:
The MEMCOR S10N-v2 modules are the membrane filter portion of the submerged membrane
filtration system used at our Water Treatment Plant. They physically filter the water. The S10N-v2
modules are being provided as the direct replacement of the S10N-v1 (and S10V, previously)
modules currently in place at the WTP.
2) This is a sole source because:
MEMCOR is the sole provider of items that are compatible with existing equipment, inventory,
systems, programs or services. The City currently has a 20-year CPI based fixed replacement cost
contract in place that is set to expire in June of 2024.
3) What necessary features does this vendor/ manufacturer provide which are not available
from other vendors/ manufacturers? Be specific:
The physical parameters of the S10N-v2 modules match specifically to the infrastructure currently in
place at the Water Treatment Plant. Other manufacturers do not currently make an alternative;
MEMCOR is the sole producer of our membrane system. Other manufacturers produce submerged
style filtration systems but they are engineered differently.

attachments.text:
Water Treatment Plant (WTP)
Improvements
Phase 1 Upgrade 23/24 (underway)
Phase 2 Upgrade 24/25 (planned)
June 18, 2024
Jeremy J. Lustig, PE, Utility Services Manager
1
Water Treatment Plant - background
￿ In 2019, the City of Kennewick (City) completed a Water
Treatment Plant (WTP) condition assessment that
primarily focused on the evaluation of critical operating
assets and to identify their anticipated useful life.
￿ The condition assessment identified several components
in need of replacement as well as, identified methods for
increasing water treatment plant production capacity.
￿ Additional water supply need triggered in 2021 when total
water supply/ production exceeded 90% of available
(with ASR assumed offline)
2
Historic Max Day Water Supply
3
Water Supply Projections
4
WTP Phase 1 Upgrade 23/24 (underway)
Phase 1 consists of the following improvements currently
underway (primarily “condition based” improvements):
￿ Chemical feed and bulk storage tank replacements
￿ Pre-procurement @ ~$700k, PO issued September 2023
￿ Surge tank upgrade (existing and future capacity)
￿ Pre-procurement @ ~$170k, PO issued May 2023
￿ Sedimentation basin cleaning access catwalk
5
WTP Phase 2 Upgrade 24/25 (planned)
Phase 2 will consists of the following improvements
(“condition based” and “capacity based” improvements):
￿ Variable Frequency Drives (VFDs) – electrical motor cntrls
￿ Pre-procurement @ ~$260k, PO issued March 2023
￿ Vertical Turbine Pumps (increased capacity)
￿ Pre-procurement @ ~$740k, PO issued May 2023
￿ Electrical Switch Gear (increased capacity)
￿ Pre-procurement @ ~36k, PO issued May 2024
￿ Filtrate Permeate Pumps (increased capacity)
￿ Pre-procurement @ $820k, PO issued May 2024
￿ Membranes*
6
WTP Phase 2 – Membranes
The last pre-procurement item for the phase 2 upgrade are
the individual membrane modules (“condition and capacity”
based). Replace existing modules and also expand each
filter cell to max out full treatment/ production.
￿ Membrane filter modules x 2,304 (and components)
￿ Pre-procurement @ ~$1.9 million
The City has an existing 20-year CPI based pricing agreement
with Memcor which expires in June 2024. Last chance to
purchase under guaranteed pricing.
7
WTP Improvements
Key take-aways:
￿ Upon completion of Phase 2, the WTP will have increased
treatment capacity of ~ 20 million gallons per day
(an increase of 5 mgd)
￿ The additional water capacity increase is projected to
provide through 2040 (15 years), depending on growth
￿ The WTP (and Ranney Collectors) are the “heart” of the
City’s water supply system
￿ Future capital projects are also planned to address
efficient conveyance of that additional capacity
￿ Transmission pipelines in Zone 1 (where the WTP pumps to)
8
Questions?
